record.what_it_does: Web search, scrape, crawl and browser-interaction API that returns LLM-ready Markdown/JSON.
record.auth_notes: The REST API (https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2) uses one auth scheme: the OpenAPI spec's securitySchemes defines only bearerAuth (type http, scheme bearer), which carries the dashboard API key as `Authorization: Bearer fc-...`. Keyless use is allowed for search, scrape, parse and interact, capped per IP per day. Crawl, map, extract and batch scrape need a key. OAuth sign-in exists only for the hosted MCP server (/v2/mcp-oauth). It is not an OAuth flow for the REST API, so it is not listed. A multi-user toolkit would have each user supply their own API key.
record.access_notes: The free plan is $0, needs no credit card and gives 1,000 credits a month. Free-plan rate limits are 10 requests per minute for scrape, map and search, and 2 per minute for crawl and agent. Paid plans are Hobby $19, Standard $99, Growth $399, Scale $749 (monthly) and Enterprise (custom). No app review or approval is needed.
record.api_breadth_notes: The v2 OpenAPI spec lists about 60 or more operations. They cover scrape (plus job get and interact), batch scrape, crawl (start, status, cancel, errors, active, params-preview), map, search (plus developer, gov and research-paper search, and feedback), extract, agent (plus trace and snapshots), interact/browser sessions (create, execute, delete, list), parse, monitor (full CRUD, run and checks), and team usage, credit and queue endpoints. I read about 60% of the spec, so the count is a minimum.
record.mcp_notes: Vendor-hosted servers: https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp (API key as a bearer token, or keyless for search, scrape and parse) and https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth (OAuth browser sign-in). The docs also link a guide to run the server locally (firecrawl-mcp).
record.blocker_notes: API keys are self-serve on a free tier, and there is a published OpenAPI spec. The only friction is the low free-plan rate limits (2 to 10 requests per minute) and credit-based metering, with each user needing their own key.
